title.narrative: NDI Ukraine "Promoting Inclusion and Combatting Discrimination" 2021-2024
NDI Ukraine "Promoting Inclusion and Combatting Discrimination" 2021-2024

description.narrative:
Objectives
This is a 36-month project with four objectives:
Objective 1 - Increase the capacity of key governmental bodies tasked with promoting gender-responsive approaches to policymaking.
Intermediate Result 1.1 Gender advocates, including parliament, government bodies, and CSOs demonstrate increased collaboration to advance gender equality.
Objective 2 - Increase public understanding of the benefits of gender equality at the national level.
Intermediate Result 2.1 Ukrainian citizens have increased exposure to gender-responsive messaging.
Objective 3 LGBTQ CSOs promote increased tolerance of LGBTQ people through sustained outreach and advocacy campaigns.
Intermediate Result 3.1 - LGBTQ CSOs form coalitions around shared priorities to advocate for legislative changes and/or corporate policies and practices to support LGBTQ people.
Intermediate Result 3.2 LGBTQ CSOs broaden support base for LGBTQ inclusion through evidence-based public outreach efforts to combat discrimination toward LGBTQ people.
Intermediate Result 3.3 - Improve CSOs ability to sustain efforts combating discrimination toward LGBTQ people.
Objective 4 - Gender equality and LGBTQ inclusion movements jointly address intersectional issues.
Intermediate Result 4.1 - Leaders of the LGBTQ inclusion and the gender equality movements partner to expand their networks.

The goal of the project is to promote greater inclusion in Ukraine’s political processes among women and members of the LGBTQ+ communities. This is a 36-month program with four objectives:
Objective 1 - Increase the capacity of key governmental bodies tasked with promoting gender-responsive approaches to policymaking.
Objective 2 - Increase public understanding of the benefits of gender equality at the national level.
Objective 3 – LGBTQ+ CSOs promote increased tolerance of LGBTQ+ people through sustained outreach and advocacy campaigns.
Objective 4 - Gender equality and LGBTQ+ inclusion movements jointly address intersectional issues.

The goal of the project is to promote greater inclusion in Ukraine’s political processes among women and members of the LGBTQ+ communities. This is a 36-month program with four objectives:
Objective 1 - Increase the capacity of key governmental bodies tasked with promoting gender-responsive approaches to policymaking.
Objective 2 - Increase public understanding of the benefits of gender equality at the national level.
Objective 3 – LGBTQ+ CSOs promote increased tolerance of LGBTQ+ people through sustained outreach and advocacy campaigns.
Objective 4 - Gender equality and LGBTQ+ inclusion movements jointly address intersectional issues.

- NDI conducted a gender-specific national survey from December 2023-March 2024 entitled Ensuring Equal Rights and Opportunities for Women and Men in Ukrainian Society. Survey topics included: perceptions of gender equality; gender roles during wartime; gender-based discrimination; and gender-based violence (GBV). Results of the survey found that 74% of respondents consider equality between men and women to be important, and 46% believe that women are more involved in volunteer activities than men. However, at the same time, 57% of respondents believe that women are actively involved in the defense of the country, but only 40% in political activity - reflecting the continued perception of traditional gender roles in Ukraine. Overall, the survey results demonstrate significant progress in understanding the importance of gender equality among Ukrainian men and women, but show that there is still more work to be done in helping women overcome stereotypes that limit their participation in areas such as politics and defense.
- NDI and NAUCS launched the School of Gender Mainstreaming, a comprehensive online educational program for civil servants to increase their awareness of gender-responsive governance, gender aspects of the civil service, and how to improve institutional mechanisms for implementing gender policy. In June 2024, NAUCs officially added the NDI course to their online professional development platform. Civil servants will be required to take the course as part of their professional development program cycle, however, it was then found that many civil servants had already successfully completed the course at their own initiative.
- NDI also supported the fifth, sixth, and seventh national annual Ukrainian Women's Congresses (UWC). The annual UWCs provide a critical platform to spotlight both the achievements and challenges for gender equality in Ukraine, and to show how gender equality contributes to Ukraines resilience and that womens perspective and leadership in political and social processes is critical for Ukraines future. Panel discussions during the events focused on topics such as womens participation in politics and decision-making, the role of women in local politics, women in security and defense, and key achievements of the Ukrainian government and society in advancing gender equality throughout the past 30 years of Ukraine's independence.
- NDI provided financial support to the Regional Press Development Institute (RPDI), in conducting awareness-raising activities at the national level aimed at increasing public understanding of the benefits of gender equality. With NDI support, RPDI operates the Povaha and Women are 50% of Ukraines Success websites, through which they publish materials to foster public discussion on the benefits of gender equality, increase visibility of emerging women leaders, and highlight the contributions of Ukrainian women in the military, volunteer, political, and diplomatic sectors.
- In order to increase the visibility and empowerment of the LGBTQI community in Ukraine, NDI issued subawards to six LGBTQI CSOs, to support their capacity development and outreach efforts. Throughout the duration of the program, NDI provided all six selected partners with targeted technical, financial, and capacity building support. Capacity building support included sharing NDI and external research findings with partners to boost LGBTQI advocacy efforts, ongoing communication on relevant opportunities, and consultations on project design for diversified funding.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
